data.name: Cosmas
data.gender_notes: Cosmas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word kosmos, meaning 'order', 'arrangement', or 'ornament'. In the New Testament, Cosmas and Damian were two Christian saints who were twin brothers, physicians, and martyrs. The name Cosmas carries the meaning “Grace, beauty, order” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Cosmas usually hope their child will grow to embody grace, beauty, order and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes harmony, balance, and the divine order.
data.etymology: Cosmas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Grace, beauty, order.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cosmas total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_english.meaning: meaning gift of order, free, healthy, and beautiful soul
in_english.long_meaning: Cosmas, a name of Greek origin, meaning gift of order, free, healthy, and beautiful soul, coming from the Greek word κοσυμπσ, kosmos, meaning universe, world, or order, and the suffix ας, as, meaning gift, and implying a gift from God, a name associated with virtues such as order, freedom, health, and beauty, and with the saint Cosmas, a martyr and a companion of Saint Damian, venerated in the Orthodox Church.

data.cultural_impact: The name Cosmas is of Greek origin and holds the meaning 'order', 'arrangement', or 'ornament'. This name was popular among the ancient Greeks and was also chosen by the early Christians as a tribute to Cosmas and Damian, the patron saints of medicine. The name has since been carried throughout history, even extending beyond Europe to other parts of the world, and is a testament to the influential reach of Greek culture and the enduring legacy of the early Christian saints.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Cosmas holds a deep spiritual significance for Christians, as it is the name of one of the greatest and most revered early Christian saints. Cosmas and his twin brother Damian are known as the 'Apostles of Asia', as they were born in Cilicia (modern-day Turkey) and are believed to have spread Christianity throughout the region. They are also known as the 'Anargyroi', or the 'Silver-less One', as they were said to have rejected payment for their medical services. The name Cosmas, therefore, serves as a reminder of the virtues of compassion, selflessness, and dedication to healing and serving others.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cosmas, derived from the Greek word 'kosmos' meaning universe or order, symbolizes a harmonious balance between the divine and the material world in a Christian context. It suggests a connection to the cosmos and the divine order, reflecting the belief in the interconnectedness of all creation.

historical_references.reference: Cosmas of Aetna, a legendary bishop and martyr, was said to have lived during the 3rd century. According to a popular legend, he was discovered buried in a cave on Mount Etna in Sicily by Saint Boniface of Rome and Saint Heliodorus of Apamea, who were on a pilgrimage to Sicily. His relics were reportedly miraculous and attracted many pilgrims.
historical_references.context: Legendary martyr, discovery of his relics during a pilgrimage

historical_references.reference: Cosmas Indicopleustes, a 6th-century Syriac Christian author, wrote a significant work titled 'Christian Topography'. In this work, Cosmas proposed a theory of the universe that placed Jerusalem, rather than Rome, at its center. He also described extensive travel to India and Ethiopia, making him one of the earliest known Europeans to have traveled to India.
historical_references.context: Syriac Christian author, significant work 'Christian Topography', extensive travel to India and Ethiopia

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Cosmas continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Mary Cosmas in Jerusalem, Israel credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Cosmas, which means "Grace, beauty, order". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
